struck: The HOA fee and a special assessment count against the rent.
use: The HOA fee counts against the rent, and a special assessment can count too; ask your lender.

struck: Using the home yourself for more than 14 days in the coming year makes the loan consumer credit, not a business loan.
use: If you expect to stay in the home more than 14 days in the coming year, federal rules no longer treat it as a rental the owner does not live in, and the business-loan exemption may not apply. Tell your lender early.

struck: Most published programs ask for 1.00 or more; some want 1.15 or 1.25 for a nightly rental or a small loan.
use: The three program sheets we read ask for a ratio of 1.00 or more, and some ask 1.15 for a nightly rental or 1.25 on a small loan.

struck: You need a score in the high 600s and up.
use: The program sheets we read set credit score floors from 660 to 720.

struck: Published programs count 80 percent of nightly-rental income.
use: Two of the three program sheets we read count at most 80 percent of nightly-rental income; the third asks for a 1.15 ratio instead.

struck: A rental in South Carolina is taxed on 6 percent of its value; a home you live in on 4 percent.
use: A home that is not its owner's legal residence, such as a house rented out year-round or a second home, is taxed on 6 percent. A legal residence rented out more than 72 days in a calendar year loses the 4 percent rate.

struck: HUD's fair market rent for the ZIP code is set at the 40th percentile of rent plus utilities in that ZIP code.
use: HUD sets its fair market rent at the 40th percentile of rent plus utilities for a standard unit across the metro area, then adjusts it for each ZIP code.

struck: At 80 percent it is still about 102 percent.
use: (cut it: on AirROI's November 5 update the 80 percent case falls to about 96 percent)

struck: The middle two-bedroom nightly rental in the Myrtle Beach area took in about $20,100 in a year.
use: The middle two-bedroom nightly rental in the Myrtle Beach area took in about $20,100 in a year, counting listings open only part of the year.

struck: All DSCR programs close inside an LLC or a corporation.
use: A DSCR loan can close in your name or in an LLC; the investor clients we work with usually close in an LLC.

struck: Carolina Forest: almost no flood zone, and new homes.
use: Almost no houses in Carolina Forest are in FEMA's high-risk flood zone.
